title: The Crown of Ashvale
premise: Yara Montrose has spent her whole life in Ashvale, a valley where magic cannot follow, serving as a mercenary for a god who stopped answering prayers a generation ago. When the old gods suddenly begin answering again — and her silent god speaks through the mouth of a dying stranger — Yara learns that Ashvale is not a refuge but a prison: a country erased from memory by the surviving gods to hide their greatest crime. To free her people and her god, she must find the Door out of a country that no longer exists, guided by a found family of exiles, heretics, and one very stubborn cartographer. In the end, Yara chooses justice over restoration: she opens the Door but refuses to restore the old order, unmaking the gods' claim on memory so that Ashvale's people — not their rulers — decide what the world remembers.
about_author: Yara Marchetti is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing suppressed regional histories before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people whom official records forgot, and she insists every one of her novels contains at least one accurate antique map.

chapters.title: The God Who Stopped Speaking
chapters.summary: POV Yara. On the eve of the long winter, Yara takes a contract guarding a shrine to her silent god, Veyra, whose altar has been cold for thirty years. A dying pilgrim stumbles in speaking words that are not his own. The beat: weary duty cracking open into dread as the dead man's mouth says Yara's name.

chapters.title: Ashes on the Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Yara. The mercenary company's ledger shows contracts going unpaid; winter is coming and coin is thin. Yara argues with her captain, Bren, about taking a forbidden job escorting a stranger toward the valley's edge. Beat: loyalty strained by hunger, and the first hint that leaving Ashvale is unthinkable — or impossible.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Nowhere
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Odile, an exile cartographer who draws maps of places that 'don't exist,' arrives in Ashvale claiming the valley appears on no chart in the world. She hires Yara privately. Beat: wary fascination between two women who both suspect the world has been lying to them.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered
chapters.summary: POV Yara. Across the valley, shrines flare with answered prayers for the first time in living memory — small miracles, wrong miracles. Veyra's altar stays dark while other gods grow loud. Beat: hope curdling into unease; the old gods are awake, and they are looking for something.

chapters.title: What the Elders Buried
chapters.summary: POV Bren. Bren breaks into the company's sealed archive and finds records older than the valley itself: muster rolls from a country called Ashvale that fell, not was founded. Beat: quiet horror as he realizes everyone's grandparents lied, and he must decide whether to tell Yara.

chapters.title: The Edge of the Map
chapters.summary: POV Yara. Yara, Odile, and Bren travel to the valley's rim, where fog stands like a wall and birds refuse to cross. Odile's compass spins; Yara's god-mark burns. Beat: claustrophobic wonder — the world ends here, and it ends on purpose.

chapters.title: A Voice Through the Cold
chapters.summary: POV Yara. At the rim, Veyra finally speaks: fragmentary, guilty, begging Yara to find 'the Door' before the winter finishes falling. She reveals Ashvale was hidden, not saved. Beat: betrayal and grief — Yara's lifelong faith was built on a prison wall.

chapters.title: The Heretic's Kitchen
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The trio shelters with Sefa, an old woman who keeps banned rites in her kitchen and remembers fragments of the fallen country through songs. Beat: warmth and found family taking root around a hearth, even as Sefa warns that remembering is how the gods find you.

chapters.title: Hunters in White
chapters.summary: POV Bren. Pale riders arrive wearing the faces of answered prayers — servants of the loud gods hunting anyone who carries true memory. The company scatters; Sefa burns her relics and stays behind. Beat: first real loss, and the cost of knowing made flesh.

chapters.title: The Song Under the Floorboards
chapters.summary: POV Yara. Following Sefa's song, the survivors find a buried chapel where the walls remember: murals depicting the Door, guarded by 'the one who chose silence.' Beat: revelation — Veyra hid Ashvale herself, to protect something, or someone.

chapters.title: Why She Went Silent
chapters.summary: POV Yara. In the chapel, Veyra confesses fully: the gods committed an atrocity at the world's founding, and she hid Ashvale's people rather than let them be witnesses executed. Hiding them required erasing the country — and her own voice. Beat: Yara's faith shatters and re-forms around anger and terrible understanding.

chapters.title: The Company Divides
chapters.summary: POV Bren. Word spreads; some mercenaries want to bargain with the loud gods for safety, others to fight. Bren holds a bitter council in the snow. Beat: found family fracturing under pressure, with Bren choosing Yara's side at personal cost.

chapters.title: The Toll of Names
chapters.summary: POV Odile. To open the Door, they need true names of the erased country — held in the loud gods' archive beyond the fog. Odile volunteers to infiltrate using her forged credentials as an imperial surveyor. Beat: fear worn as competence; Odile walks into the lion's den alone.

chapters.title: The Archive of Small Gods
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Inside the gods' mountain archive, Odile discovers the stolen names — and something worse: plans to let the long winter finish falling and bury Ashvale forever. She barely escapes with a name-fragment. Beat: triumph shadowed by a ticking clock.

chapters.title: Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: POV Yara. The deep cold arrives early and wrong; crops die, the fog wall creeps inward. Refugees flood toward the chapel. Beat: desperation binding strangers into a makeshift family, with Yara reluctantly becoming their leader.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Bren. A faction of mercenaries sells the chapel's location to the pale riders to buy passage out. Bren confronts his oldest friend among them. Beat: heartbreak and resolve; some betrayals come from love of home, which makes them worse.

chapters.title: Stand at the Buried Chapel
chapters.summary: POV Yara. The riders assault the chapel while Odile works the name-fragment into the Door's lock. Yara holds the line beside Bren and the refugees. Beat: sacrificial courage — the company bleeds for people they met weeks ago.

chapters.title: The Door Out of a Country That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: POV Yara. The Door opens onto the memory of Ashvale before the fall — sunlit, whole, full of the dead. Veyra offers to restore everything if Yara steps through and becomes the country's new keeper-god. Beat: temptation at its most seductive; the climax begins.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: POV Yara. Instead of restoring the old order, Yara drags the surviving loud gods before the Door and forces them to witness what they buried. She demands not vengeance but surrender: the right of the living to keep their own memories. Beat: righteous fury tempered into judgment — the theme made action.

chapters.title: The Unmaking of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Odile rewrites the Door's names, dissolving the veil instead of opening it: Ashvale rejoins the world, and the gods lose their monopoly on memory. Veyra fades, finally at peace, thanking Yara. Beat: bittersweet transcendence; the cost is the god Yara loved.

chapters.title: What the World Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Bren. Spring comes impossibly fast. The outside world meets Ashvale; some welcome it, some grieve the lost isolation. Bren rebuilds the company as something new — guards of the Door's threshold, sworn to no god. Beat: quiet rebuilding, grief settling into scar tissue.

chapters.title: The Crown of Ashvale
chapters.summary: POV Yara. Offered a crown by grateful elders, Yara refuses and instead plants Veyra's cold altar-stone in the town square as a memorial. With Odile and Bren beside her, she maps the road forward. Beat: resolution — found family, chosen memory, and a future owned by no one but the living.
